subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: The purpose and nature of business

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the four factors of production?
questions.explain: The four factors of production are land, labour, capital and enterprise.

questions.q: A business buys wood for GBP 20 and sells a finished chair for GBP 75. How much value has been added?
questions.explain: Added value is the difference between the selling price and the cost of bought-in inputs, here GBP 75 minus GBP 20.

questions.q: What is meant by 'opportunity cost'?
options: The next best alternative given up when a choice is made
The total fixed costs of running a business
The cost of borrowing money from a bank
The money left after all costs are paid
questions.explain: Opportunity cost is the benefit of the next best alternative that is sacrificed when a decision is made.

questions.q: Which statement best explains the difference between a good and a service?
options: A good is a physical product, whereas a service is an intangible activity
A good is always cheaper than a service
A good is sold only online, whereas a service is sold in shops
A good produces no profit, whereas a service does
questions.explain: Goods are tangible physical items, while services are intangible actions performed for customers.

questions.q: Which of the following is a common characteristic of a successful entrepreneur?
questions.explain: Entrepreneurs typically show risk-taking, determination and organisation when setting up a business.

questions.q: Which form of business ownership gives the owner unlimited liability?
questions.explain: A sole trader has unlimited liability, meaning personal assets can be used to pay business debts.

questions.q: What does 'limited liability' mean for the shareholders of a company?
options: They can only lose the amount they invested in the business
They are not responsible for any of the company's debts at all
They must repay all company debts from personal savings
They are limited to owning one share each
questions.explain: Limited liability means owners' losses are restricted to the sum they invested; personal assets are protected.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a private limited company (Ltd) and a public limited company (plc)?
options: A plc can sell its shares to the general public on the stock exchange, an Ltd cannot
An Ltd has limited liability, a plc has unlimited liability
A plc must have only one owner, an Ltd must have several
An Ltd pays no tax, a plc pays corporation tax
questions.explain: Public limited companies can trade shares publicly on the stock exchange, whereas private limited company shares are sold privately.

questions.q: In a franchise agreement, which statement is correct?
options: The franchisee pays the franchisor a fee and/or royalties to use an established brand
The franchisor pays the franchisee to run the brand
The franchisee owns the brand and sells it to the franchisor
The franchisor has unlimited liability for the franchisee's debts
questions.explain: A franchisee buys the right to trade under an established brand, paying the franchisor an initial fee and ongoing royalties.

questions.q: Two friends want to start a business together, share the profits and responsibilities, but do not want the cost of forming a company. Which ownership type suits them best?
questions.explain: A partnership allows two or more people to share ownership, profits and responsibilities without incorporating.

questions.q: Which of the following is a common financial aim of a business?
questions.explain: Profit maximisation, along with survival and growth, is a typical business objective.

questions.q: Why is 'survival' often the main objective for a newly started business?
options: Because new firms face high risks and strong competition in their early period
Because new firms are legally banned from making a profit
Because survival guarantees the largest market share immediately
Because survival removes the need for a business plan
questions.explain: New businesses prioritise survival because they are vulnerable to cash-flow problems and competition when starting out.

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-financial business objective?
questions.explain: Social, ethical and environmental goals are non-financial objectives, unlike profit, revenue or cost targets.

questions.q: An established business has recently paid off its debts and now wants to open new branches in other towns. Which objective is it most likely pursuing?
questions.explain: Expanding into new locations reflects a growth objective, common once a firm is financially secure.

questions.q: Which of the following is an internal stakeholder of a business?
questions.explain: Employees work within the business, making them internal stakeholders, unlike external groups such as suppliers or government.

questions.q: Which of the following is a likely objective of a business's employees as stakeholders?
questions.explain: Employees are chiefly interested in secure jobs, fair wages and good working conditions.

questions.q: A factory decides to extend its opening hours into the night to increase output. Which stakeholder group is most likely to object due to noise?
questions.explain: Local residents are affected by noise and disruption, so their objectives can conflict with the firm's push for higher output.

questions.q: Why might the objectives of shareholders and customers conflict?
options: Shareholders may want higher prices to raise profit, while customers want lower prices
Shareholders and customers always share exactly the same aims
Customers want lower profits, while shareholders want higher prices only for suppliers
Shareholders want to pay more tax, while customers want less choice
questions.explain: Shareholders often seek higher profits through higher prices, which conflicts with customers' desire for low prices.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key factor a business considers when choosing its location?
options: Proximity to the market and customers
The colour of the company logo
The number of letters in the business name
questions.explain: Nearness to customers, labour, materials and low site costs are all important location factors.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a business plan?
options: To set out the business's aims and how it will achieve them, often to obtain finance
To guarantee that the business will make a profit
To replace the need for any market research
To avoid paying tax to the government
questions.explain: A business plan outlines objectives, strategy and finances, and is frequently used to secure funding from lenders or investors.
